title: Marrakech or Seville in winter: which is better?
author: Brogan
intro: Marrakech and Seville are two of the best winter city breaks within four hours of the UK, and both are often sunny when Britain isn't. Marrakech is a little warmer by day, more exotic and usually cheaper. Seville is easier, gentler and full of orange trees and tapas bars. Here's how to choose.
seo_title: Marrakech or Seville in winter? How they compare
seo_description: Marrakech is about 18-20°C in winter, Seville 16-18°C. Weather, sights, food, costs and flights compared, with a verdict for each kind of trip.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Warmer by day:** Marrakech, just
- **Easier first trip:** Seville
- **More exotic:** Marrakech
- **Better for food and bars:** Seville

Both make a great three or four-day winter break. Pick Marrakech for souks, riads, the Atlas Mountains on the horizon and a real change of scene. Pick Seville for a relaxed, walkable city of palaces, flamenco and tapas, where everything feels easy.

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.text:
| | [Marrakech](/destinations/marrakech) | [Seville](/destinations/seville) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| December high | about 19°C | about 17°C |
| January high | about 18°C | about 16°C |
| February high | about 20°C | about 18°C |
| Winter nights | cold, near 5°C | cool |
| Time difference | 0 to +1 hr | +1 hr |
| Flight from London | about 3¾ hrs | about 2½ hrs |
| Best for | souks, riads, day trips | palaces, tapas, flamenco |

The temperatures are average daytime highs from our guides. Both are dry and sunny on most winter days, but cold once the sun goes down, so pack a warm jumper and a coat.

sections.heading: Marrakech in winter
sections.text:
Winter is one of the best times to visit Marrakech, when the heat of summer has gone and the snowy Atlas Mountains stand out behind the city on clear days.

- **The medina:** the souks, the Jemaa el-Fnaa square at dusk, and the Ben Youssef Madrasa.
- **Gardens and palaces:** the Jardin Majorelle, the Bahia Palace and the Saadian Tombs.
- **Day trips:** the Ourika Valley and the Atlas foothills, the Agafay desert, or the coast at [Essaouira](/destinations/essaouira).

Local knowledge: Ramadan is expected to start in early February 2027. Sights stay open, but some cafés and restaurants outside hotels close by day, and it's polite not to eat or drink in the street before sunset. Our [Marrakech in 3 days](/blog/marrakech-in-3-days) plan has a full itinerary.

sections.heading: Seville in winter
sections.text:
Seville is one of the warmest cities in mainland Europe in winter, and its orange trees are heavy with fruit from about December to February.

- **Sights:** the Real Alcázar palace and gardens, the cathedral and its Giralda tower, and the Plaza de España.
- **Evenings:** tapas in Triana and the Alfalfa area, and flamenco in small bars and dedicated halls.
- **Day trips:** Córdoba and its Mezquita, about 45 minutes away by high-speed train.

It's an easy city to walk round, and it feels relaxed in winter, without the crowds and fierce heat of summer. Our [Seville in 3 days](/blog/seville-in-3-days) plan has a full itinerary, and [Seville or Granada in winter](/blog/seville-or-granada-in-winter) compares it with another Andalucían favourite.

sections.heading: Costs, comfort and practicalities
sections.text:
- **Where to stay:** in Marrakech, a riad in the medina, a traditional house built around a courtyard. Check that it has heating, as winter nights are cold. In Seville, anywhere in or near the old centre is walkable.
- **Money:** Seville uses the euro. In Morocco you change money or use a cash machine on arrival, as dirhams are hard to get in the UK.
- **Costs:** eating out and riads are usually cheaper in Marrakech, though guides, taxis and souk shopping add up.
- **Entry:** UK passport holders don't need a visa for a holiday in Morocco or Spain. Check GOV.UK's travel advice before you book.

Watch out: Marrakech's medina can be full on, with motorbikes in the alleys, persistent touts and haggling for almost everything. Agree taxi fares before you set off, and politely ignore anyone offering to show you the way.

sections.heading: Getting there from the UK
sections.text:
- **Marrakech:** has direct flights from many UK airports, with airlines including Ryanair, easyJet, Jet2 and British Airways, in about three and a half to four hours. The airport is about 15 minutes from the medina.
- **Seville:** has direct flights from London, including Vueling from Gatwick and Heathrow and Wizz Air from Luton, plus routes from some regional airports, in about two and a half hours.

Check which airlines fly from your nearest airport for your dates, as some routes are seasonal or don't fly every day.

sections.heading: Which should you choose?
sections.text:
- **Choose Marrakech** for a little more warmth, a real change of scene, souks and riads, and lower prices for food and stays.
- **Choose Seville** for an easy, relaxed break, palaces, tapas and flamenco, with no culture shock.
- **For a first trip abroad with children:** Seville is gentler.
- **For a couple wanting something different:** Marrakech, with a night or two in the Atlas or the desert.

Still choosing? See our [Seville or Málaga in winter](/blog/seville-or-malaga-in-winter) and [is Marrakech warm in January?](/blog/is-marrakech-warm-in-january) posts. Can't agree? Add both to somewhere.party, vote with points and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Is Marrakech or Seville warmer in winter?
faqs.answer: Marrakech is usually about 2°C warmer by day, at 18 to 20°C from December to February, compared with 16 to 18°C in Seville. Both are cold at night, Marrakech more so.

faqs.question: Is Marrakech cheaper than Seville?
faqs.answer: Usually, for food and places to stay. Guides, taxis and shopping can add up, so set a budget for the souks.

faqs.question: Is Marrakech good for a first trip to Morocco in winter?
faqs.answer: Yes. Winter is one of the best times to go, with sunny days and no summer heat. Stay in a riad with heating, and take a day trip into the Atlas Mountains.

faqs.question: How long is the flight to Marrakech or Seville?
faqs.answer: About three and a half to four hours to Marrakech, and about two and a half hours to Seville, from London.
